description_en: A wave-carved basalt outcrop on Jeju City's north shore that looks like a dragon's head rising from the sea, a few minutes from the airport. A short walk east brings you to Yongyeon, a narrow emerald pond in a cliff gorge crossed by a lit wooden suspension bridge (Yongyeon Cloud Bridge) that is popular for evening strolls.
image_source: 한국관광공사 (TourAPI 대표이미지, 공공누리 제1유형) - photographer not stated

description_en: The reconstructed seat of Jeju's Joseon-era provincial government, a walled compound of red-pillared halls and pavilions in the old city center. Next to its gate stands Gwandeokjeong, a 15th-century pavilion that is one of the oldest surviving buildings on the island.
image_source: 한국관광공사 (TourAPI 대표이미지, 공공누리 제1유형) - photographer not stated
opening_hours: 09:00-18:00 (last entry 17:30). Seasonal night opening May 1-Oct 31: 18:00-21:00, Wed-Sun only (closed Mon & Tue at night), free entry

description_en: A quiet, tree-shaded sacred site where, according to Jeju's founding myth, the three ancestors of the Tamna kingdom emerged from holes in the ground. The grounds include the three-hole depression, a shrine hall, and a small exhibition and video hall explaining the legend.
image_source: 한국관광공사 (TourAPI 대표이미지, 공공누리 제1유형) - photographer not stated
opening_hours: 09:00-18:00 (ticket sales end 17:30); opens 10:00 on Jan 1, Seollal and Chuseok

description_en: The national museum for Jeju's history and archaeology, tracing the island from prehistoric settlements and the Tamna kingdom through the Joseon era. Admission is free, and it also has an immersive media room and a children's museum.
image_source: 한국관광공사 (TourAPI 대표이미지, 공공누리 제1유형) - photographer not stated
opening_hours: 09:00-18:00 (last entry 17:30); children's museum 09:30-18:00; immersive media room 10:00-17:30

description_en: A provincial museum that explains how volcanic Jeju was formed and how islanders traditionally lived, with natural history, folk life, modern-life and marine galleries. Outside, a central garden displays rocks and stone carvings, including dol hareubang statues.
image_source: 한국관광공사 (TourAPI 대표이미지, 공공누리 제1유형) - photographer not stated
closed_days: Mon (if Mon is a public/substitute holiday, the next non-holiday); Jan 1; Seollal; Chuseok; two fumigation periods per year (e.g., closed Nov 23-24, 2026)

description_en: Jeju's biggest and longest-running permanent market, a covered maze of stalls selling seafood, tangerines, local snacks and souvenirs just a few minutes from the old city centre. In the evening a street-food night market sets up inside the market (enter around Gate 8).
opening_hours: Market approx. 07:00-21:00 (average; varies by stall). Night market: Nov-Apr 18:00-24:00, May-Oct 19:00-24:00 (stalls close early when sold out)
closed_days: none (open year-round including holidays; individual stalls vary)

description_en: A wooded volcanic hill (about 148 m) beside Jeju Port, turned into a city park with pine-shaded paths, exercise areas, a pavilion and the Mochungsa memorial grounds. Its summit is a classic spot for watching the sun set over the harbour and city.
image_source: VISITJEJU (제주관광공사) official photo - licence terms not stated

description_en: A small 67 m volcanic cone right next to Jeju International Airport, reached by a short but steep path from Doduhang port. The grassy summit gives open views of the sea, the city and landing planes, plus the popular tree-framed 'Kisses Zone' photo spot.
opening_hours: 24h / always open (no set hours; access can occasionally be restricted)

description_en: The closest swimming beach to downtown Jeju and the airport, known for its grey-sand shore and the pair of red and white horse-shaped lighthouses on the breakwater. A pine grove with a campsite sits behind the sand, and it is a favourite spot for sunsets.
opening_hours: 24h / always open (beach area). Swimming only in the official season: 2026 season was Jun 24 - Sep 6, 10:00-19:00, with night swimming Jul 15 - Aug 15 until 21:00

description_en: A free, city-run arboretum on the slopes of Gwangi Oreum in Jeju City, with themed gardens of native and subtropical plants, a bamboo grove and a forest-bathing area. Paved walking loops make it an easy green escape, and the outdoor paths stay open into the evening.
image_source: VISITJEJU (제주관광공사) official photo - licence terms not stated
opening_hours: Outdoor gardens & paths: open year-round (official site says walkable until 23:00). Indoor halls: 09:00-18:00 (Mar-Nov), 09:00-17:00 (Dec-Feb)
closed_days: Outdoor: none. Indoor halls closed on Seollal and Chuseok (the day itself)

description_en: The province's main public art museum, a low concrete building with a reflecting pool set in green foothills on the road toward Hallasan. It shows Jeju and Korean modern art plus changing special exhibitions, and has a hall for painter Chang Ri-suok's donated works.
image_source: 한국관광공사 (TourAPI / 대한민국 구석구석 관광정보 사진) - photographer and KOGL type not shown
opening_hours: 09:00-18:00 (ticketing ends 30 min before close); Jul-Sep 09:00-20:00. Temporary: during 2026 Jeju Biennale (Aug 25-Nov 15, 2026) 10:00-18:00 from Oct 1.
closed_days: Mon (if Mon is a public holiday, the next non-holiday weekday); Jan 1; Seollal; Chuseok

description_en: A shallow, calm white-sand beach with emerald water on Jeju's northeast coast, about 20 km east of the airport, backed by a lawn park and the green Seoubong hill. A paved seaside promenade and a small arched footbridge make it easy to stroll, and Seoubong's coastal trail is popular at sunset.
image_source: 한국관광공사 (TourAPI / 대한민국 구석구석 관광정보 사진) - photographer and KOGL type not shown
opening_hours: 24h / always open. 2026 swimming season Jun 24-Sep 6, swimming 10:00-19:00 (no night swimming in 2026).

name_en: Jeju 4·3 Peace Park (Jeju 4·3 Peace Memorial Hall)
description_en: A large memorial park and museum on the lower slopes east of Jeju City that remembers the tens of thousands of civilians killed during the Jeju April 3rd Incident (1947-1954). The memorial hall tells the history through six themed galleries with multilingual commentary, while the grounds hold the memorial altar, victims' name stones, and burial-site monuments.
image_source: 한국관광공사 (TourAPI / 대한민국 구석구석 관광정보 사진) - photographer and KOGL type not shown
opening_hours: Outdoor park: 24h / always open. Memorial Hall: 09:00-18:00 (last entry 17:00).
closed_days: Park: none. Memorial Hall: 1st and 3rd Monday of each month (if a public/substitute holiday, the next non-holiday day).

description_en: A cool, shady forest of tall Japanese cedars on the lower slopes east of Jeju City, laced with gentle deck and mat-covered walking paths, a mineral spring and a pond. A steeper side trail climbs Jeolmul Oreum for views toward the sea.
image_source: 한국관광공사 (TourAPI / 대한민국 구석구석 관광정보 사진) - photographer and KOGL type not shown

description_en: A cluster of eight thatched-roof buildings near Jeju Port recreating the merchant inn run by Kim Man-deok, an 18th-century Jeju businesswoman remembered for using her fortune to feed islanders during a famine. Some buildings hold a small free exhibit on old Jeju life; the others work as a traditional tavern serving local dishes. The Kim Man-deok Memorial Hall is a short walk away.
closed_days: Mon (VisitJeju; weekly vs alternate-week Mondays conflicting)

description_en: Nexon's game museum in Jeju City reopened in May 2026 after a full renovation. The old computer-history museum is now a hands-on space about players and Nexon's online games, with playable arcade and co-op zones, a retro PC gaming archive, and a MapleStory-themed café in the basement.
opening_hours: Tue-Sun 10:00-18:00 (ticket sales close 17:30; Café MapleStory last order 17:30)
closed_days: Mon; Seollal (Lunar New Year's Day); Chuseok day

description_en: A huge open-air park and museum complex in the mid-mountain forest of Jocheon, dedicated to Jeju's volcanic stone culture and the island's creation myth of Seolmundae Halmang and her 500 sons. Walking routes link a sunken stone museum, outdoor stone-statue fields, a re-created thatched-roof village, and the Seolmundae Halmang Exhibition Hall that opened in 2025.
opening_hours: 09:00-18:00 (ticket sales close 17:00); no seasonal change listed
closed_days: Mon (if Mon is a public/substitute holiday, closed the next non-holiday day instead); Jan 1; Seollal day; Chuseok day; may also close temporarily for exhibit changes or bad weather

description_en: Jeju's largest traditional market, held only every five days near the airport, with about 1,000 stalls selling produce, fresh seafood, tangerines, local snacks and household goods. Locals do their real shopping here, and there is a section where elderly women sell their own produce rent-free.
opening_hours: Market days only, approx. 08:00-18:00 (per Korea Tourism Organization data); some guides say stalls close around 19:00. Mornings are busiest.
closed_days: Opens ONLY on dates ending in 2 or 7: the 2nd, 7th, 12th, 17th, 22nd and 27th of each month, whatever the weekday. Closed (no market) on all other dates. Holiday exceptions (e.g., Seollal/Chuseok) not confirmed.

description_en: A city-run nature park on the slopes of Geochin Oreum in Bonggae-dong where Jeju's wild roe deer live in the open. A fenced viewing area and small exhibition hall near the entrance make it easy to see deer up close, and a longer forest trail loops around the oreum with views toward Hallasan.
image_source: Wikimedia Commons, 골뱅이 (via Panoramio), CC BY-SA 3.0
opening_hours: Exhibition hall & permanent observation area (상시관찰원): 09:00-18:00 (tickets until 17:00). Geochin Oreum observation trail: Mar-Oct 09:00-18:00 (tickets until 17:00); Nov-Feb 09:00-17:00 (tickets until 16:00). Entry may be limited by weather.

description_en: Jeju City's oldest downtown shopping street, once nicknamed Jeju's 'Myeong-dong', lined with clothing and shoe brand shops, cafés and small eateries. Part of it is a car-free pedestrian street, and it sits a short walk from Dongmun Market and Tapdong seafront. Nearby: about 80 m away is Jeju Central Underground Shopping Mall (제주 중앙지하상가), Jeju's only underground arcade, running beneath Jungang-ro from Dongmun Market to Gwandeokjeong with about 300 shops selling clothes, accessories and souvenirs, plus restaurants and rest areas - free to walk through, open 10:00-22:00 (varies by shop) and handy on rainy days.
image_source: 비짓제주 VISIT JEJU (제주관광공사) 제공 사진 - 공공누리 등 개방 라이선스 표시 확인 안 됨
opening_hours: Street always open; shop hours vary (roughly 10:00 to 18:00-22:00 depending on the shop)
closed_days: none (street open year-round; individual shops set their own days off)

description_en: A Yemeni/Middle Eastern restaurant run by a Yemeni chef and his Korean wife, serving mandi rice, kebab wraps, hummus and falafel, with a separately labelled vegan section and a prayer room.
closed_days: Wednesday (per Visit Jeju Muslim-friendly guide; HappyCow and Traveloka list different days, so confirm)

description_en: A small Thai-owned restaurant near Yongduam serving pad thai, rice-noodle soups and curries, where staff will make most dishes vegan on request.
A famous local soup house known for its thick Jeju-style bracken (gosari) and beef soup and for momguk seaweed-pork soup, served by the bowl from early morning.
closed_days: Listed as open year-round (연중무휴); holiday closures not confirmed

description_en: A long-running (since 2002) Jeju meat-noodle shop, now in a new building near Iho, known for pork-bone broth noodles topped with sliced boiled pork.
A large bakery café right on Hamdeok Beach, with sea-view terrace seating and coffee and pastries made with Jeju ingredients.
A busy local snack shop near Halla University known for cold yeolmu (young radish kimchi) noodles and anchovy-chili gimbap, with cheap single-portion dishes.
A quiet café in a converted old house with a hanok-style garden off Chilseong-ro, serving traditional teas, yakgwa and other Korean desserts, and coffee.

Jeju Monument No. 1: an altar on the site of the former Gyullim Seowon academy honoring five Joseon-era scholars and officials, exiled to or posted on Jeju, who advanced learning on the island. Nearby: about 80 m along the same lane is Jeju Fortress (제주성지), the old city wall, where roughly 150 m near Namsugak has been restored; most of the rest was dismantled in 1925-1928 to reclaim land at the port, so the two are easy to see together.

A spring-fed stream that runs through old downtown Jeju City past Dongmun Market to Jeju Port, lined with walking paths. The area is the start of Jeju Olle Route 18 and hosts the yearly Sanjicheon Festival.
A photography gallery made by joining and remodelling two old inn buildings beside Sanjicheon Stream, showing work by Jeju photographers and photographers who documented the island.
closed_days: Mon; public holidays; Apr 25 (foundation day); May 1 (Workers' Day)

description_en: A contemporary art museum in a former motel near Sanjicheon Stream that keeps traces of the old building while showing Korean and international contemporary art. One ticket covers this and the nearby Dongmun Motel 2.

A museum on the life of Kim Man-deok (1739-1812), a Jeju merchant who used her fortune to feed islanders during a famine, presented as Korea's first exhibition hall on the culture of sharing. Audio guides are available in English, Chinese and Japanese.
closed_days: Mon; Jan 1; Seollal and Chuseok (if Mon is a public holiday, closed the next weekday instead)

description_en: A 136 m volcanic cone next to Sarabong with a cliffside path called Jangsuro that circles it, giving views over Jeju Port, passing ships and the sea. Rocks such as Goraegul cave sit at the foot of the northern cliffs.

A green park in central Jeju City with a wide lawn, tall trees, flower beds and spring cherry blossoms. It holds a monument to the 1988 Olympic torch arrival, a 1995 time capsule and memorials including the Jeju 4.3 Haewon Bangsatap.

The province's main performing-arts and exhibition venue, run by the Jeju Culture and Arts Promotion Agency, with a main hall, small theatre and exhibition rooms showing local artists. It is also home to the provincial dance troupe.
An old residential alley in Ildo 2-dong whose house walls have been covered with murals since 2008 public-art projects, keeping the look of old Jeju City.

Site of the seaside village of Gonheul-dong, which soldiers burned on 5-6 January 1949 during the Jeju April 3 Incident, killing many residents. The village was abandoned afterwards and is now a 4.3 memorial site on the coast east of Byeoldobong.
A roughly 220 m alley above Dongmun Market painted with murals of old Jeju and its scenery, close to the Jeju Fortress wall and Ohyeondan. Seeing all the paintings takes about 30 minutes.

Jeju's first school, a Joseon-era state Confucian academy founded in 1392 and moved to this Yongdam-dong site in 1827. Its halls, including Daeseongjeon (a national Treasure), Myeongnyundang and Gyeseongsa, still stand.

A contemporary art museum set in a former cinema in Jeju's old downtown near Tapdong, left largely unrenovated so traces of the old building remain. A 5th-floor cafe and shop look over the old town and Tapdong.

A long seafront plaza and promenade on the old-downtown coast, centered on the Tapdong Beach Stage outdoor amphitheater. Locals and visitors stroll here at night and catch buskers and events in summer.

A 60-year-old traditional market in the west of the old downtown, known for meat: buy cuts at the market's butcher shops and have them grilled at the meat restaurants in the market building for a table-setting fee. It also sells groceries, dried fish and fruit.

The seaside road (officially Seohaean-ro) running from near Yongduam Rock toward Dodubong along the coast north of the airport, part of Olle Route 17. It has small parks for stopping to look at the sea, night lighting on the water, and many cafes, hotels and raw-fish restaurants.

A long seaside park on the Yongdam coastal road with open sea views, lit up at night and on Olle Route 17. Poems and murals line its benches and seawall, and a Lorelei statue marks Jeju City's friendship with Germany's Loreley.
A free seaside leisure and sports park for Jeju residents beside the airport, with sports and convenience facilities; swimming and fishing are possible in summer. Expect aircraft noise.

A multi-purpose art space in the remodeled former Jeju National University Hospital building in the old downtown, on the site of a Joseon-era government office. Its galleries show painting, sculpture, video, installation and new-media art.
An old-downtown street where Jeju's annual spring king cherry blossom festival is held, with cafes and restaurants along the way.

A small harbor that Yongdam villagers made by breaking up the rocky shore, also called Dakkeune Port. Here you can see Deungmyeongdae, an old traditional lighthouse, and a spring-water well; the village emptied after the airport expanded.

The area around Jeju City's Plaza No. 7, popularly called Haetae Hill (Haetae Dongsan), where many people were killed during the Jeju April 3rd Incident. It is now a busy junction on the road from the airport to Sinjeju.
A stretch of the Yongdam-Iho coastal road near Jeju Airport whose seawall is painted in rainbow colors; a popular seaside photo and strolling spot.
image_source: 한국관광공사 (TourAPI 대표이미지, via ktriptips.com mirror; 공공누리 type not shown on mirror)

description_en: A car-free pedestrian street in Yeon-dong, Shin-Jeju, lined with restaurants, bars, clothing and souvenir shops; formerly called Baozen Street.
image_source: 한국관광공사 (TourAPI 대표이미지, via ktriptips.com mirror; 공공누리 type not shown on mirror)

name_en: Arboretum Theme Park (Night Market Street & LED Park)
description_en: An evening spot next to Halla Arboretum where a pine grove is lit with LED lights and a night market of food trucks, flea-market stalls and busking runs.
A low forested oreum (about 117 m relative height) in Ora-dong with a wooden-deck trail to the summit and a forest loop path midway, popular with locals for walks.
A small breakwater harbor between Yongduam Coastal Road and Iho Tewoo, near Jeju Airport, known for fishing boats and with restaurants and fishing shops nearby.
image_source: 한국관광공사 (TourAPI 대표이미지, via ktriptips.com mirror; 공공누리 type not shown on mirror)

description_en: A spring of cold, clear groundwater that is the symbol of Dodu village; in summer it feeds an outdoor pool, and there is also a small spring-water bathhouse.
A tiny harbor next to Iho Beach with sea-themed murals on the breakwater, a pavilion for resting, and views of the red and white horse lighthouses; popular with anglers at night.
A roughly 1.15 km coastal road from Iho Tewoo Beach to Aljakji pebble beach, part of the Olle Route 17 area, with open sea views especially at sunset.
An indoor immersive media-art exhibition themed around a 1980s neighborhood supermarket where a mysterious door has drained Jeju's colors.
image_source: 한국관광공사 (TourAPI 대표이미지, via ktriptips.com mirror; 공공누리 type not shown on mirror)

description_en: A Jeju April 3rd (4·3) heritage site in Ora-dong, where the May 1, 1948 'Ora-ri arson incident' helped wreck the peace talks; a village walking route marks the history.

Jeju black pork restaurant opened in 2006, known for thick geun-gogi cuts (neck and pork belly) grilled over yeontan briquettes. Staff grill the meat at your table; it is served with meljeot anchovy sauce, and kimchi stew is a popular finish.

Long-running local restaurant known for momguk, Jeju's thick soup of pork broth simmered with mojaban (gulfweed) seaweed. It also serves dombe-gogi (sliced boiled pork), momguk noodles and squid sashimi.
opening_hours: Late-night; last order 03:00 (opening time not stated by source)

description_en: Old-style Jeju home-cooking restaurant popular with locals and tourists, where you can hear the Jeju dialect around you. Its specialty is gakjaegi-guk, a soybean-paste soup made with horse mackerel; it also serves seafood hot pot.

Seafood restaurant in Dodu-dong near Jeju Airport, run by a haenyeo (woman diver) owner and her family. Famous for abalone mulhoe (cold raw seafood soup with a distinctive soybean-paste broth) and abalone/seafood hot pot.
Popular early-morning restaurant with a single menu item: beef haejangguk, a hearty Korean soup often eaten as a hangover cure. Lines are common; just tell the staff how many people.
Restaurant serving Jeju home-style set meals inspired by haenyeo recipes, centered on braised wild rockfish from its own fishing boat. Most ingredients and wrap vegetables are from Jeju.

name_en: e-Geumdonji Tong-Galchi Jorim Jeju Airport Main Branch
description_en: Restaurant near Jeju Airport specializing in braised whole hairtail (galchi jorim), a classic Jeju seafood dish, plus grilled hairtail.
Noodle restaurant so popular that even locals line up, serving kalguksu (knife-cut noodles) in a deep broth made with bomal (Jeju sea snails) and seaweed.
Evening restaurant near Jeju City Hall known for raw mackerel sashimi; live mackerel is prepared quickly so it tastes fresh and rich rather than fishy. Also serves braised hairtail.

Abalone specialty restaurant with over 20 years of history on the Tapdong waterfront, known for abalone porridge and abalone hot-stone-pot rice. Breakfast is available and there is a large parking area.
opening_hours: Breakfast available; last order 20:00 (opening time not stated)

description_en: Jeju home-style seafood restaurant in Ido-dong ('gaetgeot' means seafood in Jeju dialect), known for clear sea urchin seaweed soup and bomal (sea snail) soup, served with side dishes of locally gathered seaweed.

name_en: Malgogi Research Lab Jeju Airport Branch
description_en: Restaurant near Jeju Mokgwana offering approachable takes on Jeju horse meat, such as horse meat sausage (the signature), horse meat sushi and rice bowls.
opening_hours: Break 14:30-17:30; last order 21:00 (opening time not stated)

description_en: Small, inexpensive eatery in Boseong Market known for bingtteok, a Jeju snack of thin buckwheat crepe rolled around seasoned radish, made with 100% Jeju buckwheat.
Bakery near Jeju Sports Complex selling Jeju-style barley bread: plain barley bread, red bean barley bread and mugwort bread. Bulk and parcel orders are possible.
Cafe in a downtown cafe street, famous for green tea bingsu: shaved ice with green tea powder, injeolmi rice cake and nuts, topped with a tower of green tea ice cream. Also serves coffee and cakes.
